battery.title: Battery
battery.description: Electronic waste in the form of batteries that contain hazardous chemicals.
processing: Collect them in an e-waste dropbox.
Do not mix them with regular waste.
Send them to a battery recycling facility.
Insulate the battery terminals to prevent short circuits.
impact: Contains mercury, cadmium, and lead, which are highly toxic.
Pollutes soil and water.
Has the potential to cause fires.

biological.title: Biological
biological.description: Wet organic waste such as food scraps, leaves, and rotten fruit.
processing: Turn it into compost.
Use a biopore hole or compost bin.
It can be processed into eco enzyme.
impact: Produces methane gas, which contributes to global warming.
Creates unpleasant odors and attracts pests.
Pollutes the environment if mixed with other waste.

cardboard.title: Cardboard
cardboard.description: Cardboard waste that is easy to recycle.
processing: Fold it and separate it from wet waste.
Send it to a waste bank or collector.
Recycle it into new cardboard products.
impact: Cannot be recycled if it is wet or dirty.
Increases the volume of dry waste in landfills.

clothes.title: Clothes
clothes.description: Used clothing that can still be worn or recycled.
processing: Donate clothes that are still wearable.
Upcycle them into bags, cleaning cloths, or crafts.
Recycle them through textile recycling facilities.
impact: Synthetic fibers produce microplastics.
Takes decades to hundreds of years to decompose.
The fashion industry is one of the largest contributors to waste.

glass.title: Glass
glass.description: Glass bottles or broken glass that can be 100% recycled.
processing: Separate it from other waste.
Collect and send it to a glass waste collector.
Recycle it into new glass products.
impact: Broken glass can be dangerous to humans.
Does not decompose and accumulates in landfills.

metal.title: Metal
processing: Clean it from food residue.
Crush it to save space.
Collect it for recycling.
impact: Can rust and pollute the soil.
Adds to inorganic waste in landfills.

paper.title: Paper
paper.description: Types of paper such as documents, magazines, and books.
processing: Separate it from wet waste.
Send it to a waste bank.
Recycle it back into paper products.
impact: Can rot and become unrecyclable if wet.
Increases the need for tree cutting.

plastic.title: Plastic
plastic.description: Plastic items such as PET bottles, bags, and packaging.
processing: Separate it based on its type.
Wash it before recycling.
Use plastic dropboxes or waste banks.
impact: Takes 400–1,000 years to decompose.
Breaks down into microplastics that can enter the human body.
Damages marine ecosystems.

shoes.title: Shoes
shoes.description: Used shoes made from rubber, fabric, and leather.
processing: Donate them if they are still wearable.
Upcycle them into plant pots, decorations, or creative materials.
Use shoe recycling programs.
impact: Mixed materials are difficult to decompose.
Produces microplastics.

trash.title: Trash
trash.description: Residual waste that cannot be recycled.
processing: Minimize waste production.
Separate it from recyclable waste.
Use incinerator facilities with emission control.
impact: Increases the burden on landfills.
Produces methane gas and toxic liquid waste.
Pollutes soil and water.
